That came first now.
The nearest catastrophe, and the biggest.

How to stop it, though?

An airship or a dragoon would probably drop the bomb.
Intercept that, then?

...No. Not possible.

Such extraordinary power in the bomb—the craft dropping it would presumably keep a very considerable height. To intercept it, we would have to reach that airspace.

Below it, the Silver Star's copies were occupying the sky.
Just force our way through? Very brave proposal. Where was the ability to perform it?

Suppose we did find a gap, or some way around. After that also, the bombing mission's escorts would have to be fought and defeated. Surely they weren't sending it without escorts.

No. Too little chance of success to stake everything on it.

Some other method was needed.
But what method? If force wouldn't stop them, negotiation?

Go straight into occupation headquarters and put my case personally to the commander?

...Under the present circumstances, this was less a solution and more a daydream wearing official shoes.

Something else. Some other way—

Certainly, the occupation army wanted to crush the Rokuhara government inside the castle, not the castle itself. No Rokuhara, no need to drop the bomb. That much made sense. en.text:
Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga. Moriuji's legitimate grandson. Supreme commander of Rokuhara.
Use that boy as the key, and make Rokuhara disappear...?

What was the captain thinking?
Certainly, the occupation army wanted to crush the Rokuhara government inside the castle, not the castle itself. No Rokuhara, no need to drop the bomb. That much made sense.

For the Green Dragon Society hiding behind them, perhaps it made no difference whether Rokuhara existed or not. But the society was not controlling the occupation army. Only cleverly steering it. The army's own interests could not simply be ignored. If the shogunate disappeared, the plan would come to a halt.

But a government is not a folding chair. Bring it out, put it away—how could it be so easy?

The captain's message was too brief. What exactly she meant, I couldn't see.

Probably she had spared herself the trouble of explaining modern affairs to Muramasa from beginning to end, and sent only the essentials. Very considerate. At present, I was not feeling grateful for this consideration.

—No. Wait. ◆

Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga is the key?

Assassinate the supreme commander?
No. No, that was not it.

He was far too young to carry Rokuhara on his shoulders. At present he held no actual power. Remove him, and Rokuhara would still be there.

So not kill him.
Keep him alive.

The shogunate didn't need his presence for its day-to-day functioning. Losing him would probably not kill it.
But he himself could bring it to an end.

Hand back the government.
Ask him to declare that Rokuhara was finished as the authority governing the nation.

Kuniuji Ashikaga was the shogunate's head in name only. Yes. But even in name, he was the head. An official declaration in his name would carry considerable weight... at least until the people holding the actual power denied it.

The occupation army had called Rokuhara an illegitimate government. Removing it was their stated reason for sending troops.
Achha. Then we would do what they wanted. Before them. Rokuhara would remove itself.

Then on what grounds would they keep fighting?

Ignore the announcement? Of course they could. But then they would lose too much. Their righteous-war banner, the goodwill of Yamato's people, their standing before the international community—criticism from every side.

Whoever was directing the occupation army, the British Commonwealth or the New Continent independence faction, surely that would be unacceptable. Every benefit they expected from the war could be lost.

This way, we could stop the Forged Bomb!
If Kuniuji Ashikaga himself announced the end of the Rokuhara regime!

公的宣言がなされれば、重大な意義を持つだろう……
少なくとも、実権を握る者に否定されるまでの間は。

名分として兵を動かした。

打って、六波羅自身の行動で。

　そうなっては進駐軍は戦闘続行する理由を失なくす。

国民の心象への悪影響、国際社会の批判等々、失う物
が多過ぎる。

　それは進駐軍を動かす者――大英連邦であれ新大陸
独立派であれ――にとって受け入れ難いはずだ。
